What is framed New York wall art?

Framed New York wall art refers to printed artwork depicting NYC scenes — such as the Manhattan skyline, neighbourhood streets, or city landmarks — presented as ready-to-display art prints, often sold as curated sets. At AboutWallArt, our framed New York wall art prints are produced in the UK on quality art paper using fade-resistant pigment inks, and the framed options arrive ready to hang straight out of the box. Sets of three are particularly popular for creating a gallery-style display above a fireplace or sofa, giving a cohesive, travel-inspired look without the effort of sourcing a matching frame. Whether you love the Big Apple, Manhattan, or simply the warm aesthetic of NYC-inspired illustration, these prints make it easy to bring that city energy into your home.

How to Hang a Set of 3 New York Wall Art Prints Above a Fireplace

1. Measure your wall space: Start by measuring the width of your fireplace or chimney breast. Divide this by three (for a set of three prints) to get a rough maximum width per print, then subtract around 5–8 cm per gap between them. This tells you the ideal print size before you order.

2. Mark your hanging points: Use a spirit level and pencil to mark three evenly spaced horizontal points at your chosen height — typically so the centre of each print sits roughly at eye level (around 145–150 cm from the floor). Even spacing between prints (5–8 cm) looks the most polished.

3. Hang the centre print first: Always start with the middle print, then work outward to the left and right. This keeps the arrangement symmetrical and makes it much easier to adjust if needed.

4. Step back and check: Once all three are up, step back to the other side of the room and check alignment. A small adjustment now saves a lot of fussing later. Use removable adhesive strips on lighter prints if you want flexibility to reposition.

5. Style the mantel below: Complement your new NYC wall art prints with warm accessories on the mantel — think dried autumn stems, amber glass candle holders, or a small stack of travel books — to echo the ochre and charcoal tones in the artwork.

Framed New York Wall Art Prints — Which Option Is Right for You?

Format — Unframed Print: The art print only, printed on your choice of Luster or Museum quality paper. You source and select your own frame. Perfect if you already have frames at home or want a very specific frame style.

Format — Framed Print: Your chosen art print mounted and framed, arriving completely ready to hang. Saves time and guarantees a neat, finished result. Available in multiple sizes with a choice of Luster or Museum quality paper.

Format — Wrapped Canvas: The artwork printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame — no print or glazing, just the image wrapped around the edges. Arrives ready to hang and suits a more relaxed, contemporary or rustic interior feel.

Paper finish (prints only) — Luster: A semi-sheen surface that reduces glare while keeping colours vibrant. A great all-rounder, especially in rooms with natural light or lamp light near the fireplace.

Paper finish (prints only) — Museum Quality: A premium fine-art paper with deeper, richer colour saturation. Ideal if you want the ochre and mustard tones of the autumn New York scenes to really stand out. Best suited to collectors or those who want a true fine-art feel.

What is dining room wall art decor?

Dining room wall art decor refers to prints, paintings, or illustrations chosen specifically to enhance the walls of a dining space — adding personality, colour, and atmosphere to the room where you eat, entertain, and gather. It can be a single statement piece or, as with this New York set, a coordinated group of prints that tell a visual story together. Travel-themed art is a particularly popular choice because it sparks conversation at the dinner table and brings a sense of the wider world into your everyday home.

How to Hang Dining Room Wall Art Decor: a Simple Step-by-Step

1. Measure your wall: Use a tape measure to find the width of your wall or the furniture below (such as a sideboard or dining table). Your set of three prints should ideally span roughly two-thirds of that width for a balanced, well-proportioned look.

2. Plan your layout on the floor first: Lay the three prints out on the floor in front of the wall to experiment with spacing before you put a single nail in. A gap of 5–8 cm between each print is a good starting point for a clean, gallery-style row.

3. Find the right height: The centre of your arrangement should sit at roughly eye level — approximately 145–150 cm from the floor is the standard guideline. If the prints will hang above a sideboard or table, leave around 20–25 cm of space between the furniture and the bottom of the prints.

4. Mark and hang: Use a pencil to mark your nail positions lightly on the wall, then use a spirit level to make sure everything is straight. If you have chosen the framed option, simply hang and enjoy — it arrives ready to go.

5. Step back and adjust: Once everything is up, step back across the room and check the spacing looks even from a distance. Small adjustments at this stage make a big difference to the finished result.

Unframed Print — The print is delivered flat and ready for you to frame in your own choice of frame. Ideal if you already have a frame style in mind or want to match existing frames in your dining room. Available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Framed Print — Your print arrives professionally framed and ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra shopping, no measuring, no hassle. The most convenient option if you want the set on your wall as quickly as possible. Available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a sturdy wooden stretcher frame, giving a contemporary, frameless finish. A great choice if you prefer a more textural, gallery-style look in your dining room. Available in a range of wrapped canvas size options.

Luster Art Paper — A subtle semi-sheen finish that works beautifully in most lighting conditions and brings out the warm ochre and painterly tones of this New York set particularly well.

Museum Quality Paper — A premium fine-art paper with a smooth matte finish for the richest, most gallery-worthy colour depth. Perfect if you want these prints to be a real centrepiece in your dining room.

What is travel wall art?

Travel wall art is decorative art prints that celebrate real places, cities, landmarks or travel experiences — designed to bring the spirit of a destination into your home. This set of three New York City prints, for example, depicts iconic Manhattan scenes in a warm watercolour illustration style, making them a great way to display a love of a particular city or a memorable trip. Travel wall art is hugely popular in hallways, living rooms and home offices because it adds personality and a sense of adventure to a space. The best travel art prints are versatile enough to work as a standalone feature or grouped together as a set, just like this ochre-toned NYC trio.

How to Hang a Set of Travel Wall Art Prints in Your Hallway

1. Plan your layout first: Lay all three prints on the floor in front of the wall to settle on the arrangement — a straight horizontal row works best for most hallways and suits this NYC set perfectly.

2. Find your centre point: Measure the total width of your three prints plus the gaps between them, then find the midpoint of your wall and mark it lightly with a pencil so your arrangement sits centred.

3. Set your hanging height: Aim for the centre of the prints to sit at roughly eye level — around 145–150 cm from the floor. In a hallway, this tends to feel natural whether you're walking past or pausing to look.

4. Keep gaps consistent: Use a ruler or a strip of card to keep the spacing between each print equal — 5 to 8 cm between prints is a good starting point for this set size.

5. Use the right fixings: Picture hooks or damage-free adhesive strips both work well for lighter unframed prints. For heavier framed options, a proper wall hook into a stud or with a wall plug is more secure and reassuring long-term.

Colour depth — Unframed / Framed Museum quality paper: Deepest, richest colour reproduction — ideal for showcasing the ochre and amber tones in this NYC set. aiItems.content:
What are large paintings for living room wall?

Large paintings for living room wall are oversized or statement-scale art prints designed to fill and anchor the main wall of a living space, typically displayed above a sofa, fireplace or console table. They are usually sold as single statement pieces or coordinating sets of two or three prints that together create one cohesive visual. In modern home decor, the term covers everything from canvas-wrapped prints to framed art prints on high-quality paper, and they do not need to be hand-painted originals — high-quality art prints reproduce illustrated and painted artwork with impressive fidelity. Choosing the right large wall art is one of the fastest ways to define the mood and personality of a living room, giving the space a genuine focal point that ties furniture, colour and style together.

How to Hang Large Paintings for Living Room Wall — a Simple Step-by-Step

1. Measure your wall space first: Before ordering, measure the width of the wall or the furniture beneath it. For a set of 3 prints, aim for the combined width of all three (including gaps) to cover roughly two-thirds of the sofa or sideboard width below — this creates a balanced, intentional look rather than prints that appear to float or get lost.

2. Choose your size and format: Decide whether you want unframed prints (great if you have a specific frame style in mind), framed prints (ready to hang immediately), or wrapped canvas (for a more contemporary, frame-free look). Scroll down on this page to see how each size looks in a real living room using our size-guide image.

3. Mark your hanging points carefully: Hold the centre print up to the wall first and mark its ideal position at eye level — roughly 145–150 cm from floor to the centre of the print is a good rule of thumb. Then measure outward from the centre print to position the two flanking prints with equal gaps between them (3–5 cm works well for a cohesive set).

4. Use a spirit level: Even a small tilt is very noticeable with a set of three prints in a row. Use a spirit level or a free spirit-level app on your phone to make sure all three are perfectly aligned before you fix them to the wall.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, step back across the room and check the arrangement from a distance — this is where small tweaks to height or spacing make a real difference to the final result.

Which Format Is Right for You? Comparing Your Options

Unframed Print — The print is delivered rolled or flat, ready for you to frame in your own choice of frame. Best for: buyers who already have frames, want a specific frame colour, or are ordering multiple sets and want a consistent custom-framed look throughout their home.

Framed Print — The art print arrives ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra trips to the frame shop needed. Best for: buyers who want a quick, hassle-free result and a polished, finished look immediately. Available in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, with the image wrapping around the edges. No glazing, no frame required. Best for: buyers who prefer a more contemporary, gallery-style look without the reflection of glass.

Luster Paper (for unframed and framed prints) — A semi-gloss finish that gives punchy, vivid colour with a slight sheen. Great in rooms where you want the colours to really sing.

Museum Quality Paper (for unframed and framed prints) — A premium fine-art paper with a smooth, low-sheen finish that gives greater depth and richness of colour. Particularly well-suited to illustrated and painterly artwork like this NYC autumn set, where the subtle tonal detail really benefits from a fine-art surface.

How to Hang Framed Dining Room Wall Art: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

aiItems.content:
What are hallway wall art ideas?

Hallway wall art ideas are ways to use prints, illustrations or artwork to decorate the walls of an entrance hall or corridor, turning an often-overlooked space into a welcoming and characterful part of the home. A well-chosen set of art prints can define the mood of your entire home, since the hallway is the very first thing guests — and you — see when stepping inside. Options range from a single statement print to a curated set of matching pieces hung in a row, a gallery wall of mixed sizes, or travel-themed illustrations that tell a personal story. Because hallways tend to be narrow, choosing art that is proportionate to the wall and cohesive in colour palette is key to making the space feel intentional rather than cluttered.

How to Hang Hallway Wall Art Ideas: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Measure your wall space: Use a tape measure to note the width and height of the wall section you want to fill. For a set of 3 prints in a row, add together the widths of all three prints plus your preferred gaps (around 5–8 cm each) to check the total fits comfortably.

2. Choose your print sizes: In a narrow hallway, smaller sizes such as A4 or A3 tend to look most balanced. Wider entrance halls can carry A2 or larger prints without feeling crowded. Check the size-guide image on the product page to see each size in a real hallway setting.

3. Mark your hanging points: Use a pencil to lightly mark the centre point of each print's position on the wall. A spirit level is your best friend here — run it across all three marks to make sure they're perfectly aligned before you put a single nail in.

4. Hang at eye level: The centre of each print should sit at roughly 145–150 cm from the floor — this is the standard eye-level position that feels most natural when you walk past. If your hallway is used by shorter family members or children, you can drop this slightly.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three prints are up, stand at the far end of the hallway and look at the overall effect. Small adjustments of even a centimetre can make a big difference to how balanced the set looks. Take your time — it's worth it.

Format — Framed print. Best for: those who want a complete, polished look straight away. What you receive: the print presented in a frame, arriving ready to hang with no extra shopping required.

Format — Wrapped canvas. Best for: a more relaxed, contemporary feel without the need for any frame at all. What you receive: the artwork printed and stretched over a canvas frame, ready to hang directly on the wall.

Paper quality — Luster art paper. Best for: a subtle satin sheen that makes colours appear vivid and painterly — suits the watercolour style of these NYC prints especially well.

Paper quality — Museum quality paper. Best for: a refined, matte gallery finish with excellent colour depth — ideal if you prefer a more understated, fine-art look for your hallway.

If your living room already has botanical prints, vintage-inspired pieces or a travel-gallery wall going on, this set will slot right in. What is a large picture for living room?

A large picture for living room is an oversized or multi-panel piece of wall art designed to make a real visual impact on a main living space wall — typically hung above a sofa, fireplace or console table as the room's focal point. Unlike smaller accent prints, a large living room picture anchors the whole space, adding colour, personality and a sense of considered style in one go. Sets of three prints — like a triptych — are a hugely popular format because they give the scale of a large single piece while allowing each panel to tell its own story. Choosing the right size, subject and colour palette means your large picture can tie together furniture, soft furnishings and wall colour into one cohesive, welcoming room scheme.

How to Hang a Large Picture for Living Room the Right Way

1. Measure your wall and furniture first: Note the width of your sofa or main furniture piece. Your set of prints — including any gaps between them — should span roughly two thirds of that width for a balanced, proportional look. Mark the centre point of the wall lightly with a pencil.

2. Find your hanging height: The centre of your artwork should sit at roughly eye level — around 145–150 cm from the floor — whether you're hanging above a sofa or on an open wall. If hanging above a sofa, keep the bottom edge of the prints about 15–20 cm above the sofa back to keep things feeling connected rather than floating.

3. Plan the layout before you put holes in the wall: Lay all three prints on the floor in front of the wall first. Use small pieces of painter's tape on the wall to mark the corners of each print — this lets you step back and check spacing and height before committing. Aim for equal gaps of around 3–5 cm between each panel in the set.

4. Use a spirit level: Even a small tilt is very obvious across a triptych set. Use a spirit level or a free phone app to make sure every print is perfectly straight before you tighten the fixings. Start with the centre print, then work outward to the left and right panels.

5. Step back and enjoy: Once all three are up, step back across the room — not just a metre away — to check the overall effect. Adjust any gaps if needed. Then put the kettle on and admire your handiwork.

Choosing Your Print Option: What's Right for You?

Unframed Print — The print only, on your choice of Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Perfect if you already have frames you love, or if you want to frame it yourself in a style that matches your existing décor exactly. Lightest and easiest to post; you handle the framing.

Framed Print — Your chosen print mounted and framed, arriving completely ready to hang — no extra trips to a frame shop needed. A brilliant time-saver and a great all-in-one option. Available in multiple sizes on Luster or Museum quality paper, so you still get to choose the finish that suits your room.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame — no glass, no mount, just the image itself with a contemporary gallery-wrap edge. Ready to hang straight away, and a great choice if you prefer a more relaxed, casual look over the classic framed-print feel. Available in a range of canvas sizes to suit your wall.

Luster Paper vs Museum Quality Paper — Luster has a gentle semi-sheen that makes colours vibrant and handles everyday light well; it's our most popular everyday choice. Museum quality paper is a premium fine-art option with a smoother, more refined finish — ideal for rooms with strong natural light or if you simply want the richest possible colour depth from this detailed, illustrated artwork.

aiItems.content:
What is office decor?

Office decor refers to the artwork, accessories, and design choices you use to personalise and improve the look and feel of a workspace — whether that's a home office, a studio, or a professional setting. Good office decor does more than look nice: it can make a space feel more motivating, calming, or creative depending on the pieces you choose. Wall art prints are one of the easiest and most affordable ways to transform a plain office wall into something that reflects your personality and taste. A well-chosen set of prints can also help define different zones in an open-plan space, add colour to a neutral room, or simply give you something lovely to look at during the working day.

How to Arrange Wall Art Prints for Your Office Decor

1. Measure your wall space first: Before ordering, measure the wall or area above your desk. For a set of 3 prints hung in a row, aim for the combined width (including gaps) to fill roughly two-thirds of the width of the furniture below — this looks the most balanced.

2. Choose your layout: A straight horizontal row at eye level is the classic choice for a set of 3 and works especially well in an office. Alternatively, try a slight vertical stagger for a more relaxed, creative feel. Lay the prints out on the floor first to visualise the arrangement before you put anything on the wall.

3. Mark your hanging points carefully: Use a spirit level and a pencil to mark where each print will hang. Keep the gaps between prints consistent — around 5–8 cm looks neat. 4. Consider the light in the room: Natural light from a window will make colours look their brightest. Avoid hanging prints in direct, harsh sunlight for long periods to keep colours looking fresh over time. A wall opposite a window is often the sweet spot.

5. Step back and adjust: Once the prints are up, stand back from across the room and check the spacing and height feel right. It's easy to nudge them at this stage — trust your eye as much as the tape measure.

Comparing Your Options: Which Format is Right for Your Office?

Format — Unframed Print: The print is delivered on its own, ready for you to frame or display as you like. Format — Framed Print: Arrives ready to hang straight out of the box — no need to source a frame separately. Printed on Luster or Museum quality paper and fitted into a frame, so it's the quickest and most convenient option for getting your new office decor on the wall the same day it arrives.

Format — Wrapped Canvas: The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden stretcher frame, giving a more textural, gallery feel. Paper choice — Luster: A semi-gloss finish that makes colours appear vivid and rich. Works beautifully with watercolour-style and illustrated artwork like these Paris prints. Luster paper is a popular choice for colourful, detailed art.

Paper choice — Museum quality: A premium smooth matte paper with no surface sheen. Gives a very refined, sophisticated finish — particularly lovely if your office has a clean, minimal aesthetic and you want the art to feel quietly confident rather than bold.

What is wall art living room large?

Wall art living room large refers to oversized or multi-panel art prints designed to make a bold, eye-catching statement on a living room wall — typically spanning a significant portion of the wall above a sofa, fireplace or sideboard. These pieces are sized to fill large expanses of wall that smaller prints simply cannot do justice to, giving a room a finished, considered look. A set of 3 prints is one of the most popular formats, as the three panels together create the visual impact of a large piece while remaining flexible and easy to arrange. At AboutWallArt, our large living room wall art prints are produced in the UK on high-quality paper using fade-resistant inks, so they stay looking sharp for years.

How to Hang Large Wall Art in Your Living Room

1. Measure your wall first: Hold a piece of string or use painter's tape on the wall to mark out the total width and height of all three prints together before you commit to hanging. The combined width of a set of 3 should ideally sit within two-thirds of the width of the furniture below it — this keeps things balanced and proportional.

2. Find your centre point: Mark the midpoint of your wall space and work outward from there, keeping an equal gap (around 5–8 cm works well) between each print. This ensures the set feels symmetrical and intentional rather than randomly placed.

3. Hang at eye level: The centre of each print should sit at roughly 145–150 cm from the floor — this is the standard gallery height and feels natural to the eye whether you're sitting or standing. If hanging above a sofa, leave around 15–20 cm of clear space between the top of the sofa and the bottom of the lowest print.

4. Use a spirit level: Even a small tilt is very noticeable with a set of 3 prints in a row. A spirit level (or a free level app on your phone) takes seconds and saves a lot of frustration. Mark your hanging points lightly in pencil before you hammer anything in.

5. Step back and check before fixing: Once your marks are on the wall, stand back from the room entrance and check the positioning at a distance — what looks right up close can feel off-centre from across the room. Adjust before making any holes permanent.

Unframed Print — The print is supplied on its own, giving you full flexibility to choose your own frame or mount. Great if you already have frames you love or want a very specific frame colour. Available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Framed Print — Arrives completely ready to hang straight out of the box — no frame-hunting, no measuring, no hassle. A brilliant choice if you want a clean, finished look immediately. Available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper, in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, with the image wrapping neatly around the edges. There is no need for a separate frame at all — it has a contemporary, gallery-style finish and hangs straight on the wall. Available in multiple sizes.

Luster Paper vs Museum Quality Paper — Luster paper has a subtle sheen that makes colours appear vivid and punchy — ideal if your living room gets good natural light. Museum quality paper is more matte with a fine-art feel, which suits the watercolour illustrated style of these Paris prints especially well and reduces any glare in brightly lit rooms.

aiItems.content:
What is office wall decoration?

Office wall decoration refers to any artwork, print or visual piece hung on the walls of a workspace — whether a home office, studio or corporate environment — to make the space feel more personal, inspiring and pleasant to work in. It can range from a single statement print to a curated set of art prints arranged as a gallery wall. Good office wall decoration does more than fill an empty wall; it sets the mood of a room, reflects your personality or brand, and can even help you feel more focused and motivated throughout the day. A coordinated set of prints — like a travel-themed trio — is one of the most popular choices because it brings colour, story and cohesion to a wall without requiring any design expertise.

How to Hang Office Wall Decoration: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Measure your wall space: Before you do anything, measure the width of the wall or section you want to fill. For a set of 3 prints, aim for the total width of all three prints plus roughly 5–8 cm of gap between each one to sit comfortably within that space.

2. Choose your layout: A horizontal row at eye level (roughly 145–150 cm from floor to print centre) is the most classic and effective arrangement for a set of three. Use a spirit level or the free spirit-level app on your phone to keep things straight.

3. Mark your hanging points: Cut out paper templates the same size as each print and use masking tape to position them on the wall before you commit to any nails. This saves a lot of guesswork and unnecessary holes.

4. Hang and adjust: Fix your hooks or picture nails, then hang each print and double-check they are level. Step back a few paces to see the overall effect — small adjustments at this stage make a big difference to the finished look.

5. Style around them: Once the prints are up, add a small desk plant, a neutral lamp or a few books in complementary tones beneath them to ground the display and tie the whole look together.
